cards.f: Equations for electrical power and energy
cards.b: P = IV; E = IVt (W, A, V; J, s).
Energy used by a 1 kW appliance in 1 hour: 1 kW h = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
Cost = energy in kW h × price per kW h; kW h = power (kW) × time (h).
Same current everywhere; supply p.d. is shared: V = V₁ + V₂.
1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂, or R = R₁R₂ ÷ (R₁ + R₂). Always less than the smaller resistor.
Each branch has the full supply p.d.; supply current = sum of branch currents.
The sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum of currents leaving it.

cards.f: Three advantages of lamps in parallel
cards.b: Each has full p.d. (full brightness); each can be switched independently; others stay on if one fails.
A thin wire that melts if current exceeds its rating, breaking the circuit.
Just above the normal working current of the appliance.
Opens automatically when current exceeds a set value; can be reset; faster than a fuse.
If the casing becomes live, a large current flows to earth through the low-resistance earth wire, melting the fuse and cutting off the supply.
Non-conducting outer casing so it can't become live; no earth wire needed.
Damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions, overloaded sockets/plugs/extension leads.

gaps.s: A 2.0 kW heater used for 3.0 hours transfers ___ kW h of energy.
Resistors of 4.0 Ω and 6.0 Ω in series have a total resistance of ___ Ω.
Two 6.0 Ω resistors in parallel have a combined resistance of ___ Ω.
A 230 V lamp with current 0.50 A has power ___ W.
In a series circuit the ___ is the same at every point.
A fuse contains a thin wire that ___ if the current is too large.
A fuse rating should be ___ above the normal current of the appliance.

short.q: A kettle rated 2.5 kW is used for 6 minutes. Electricity costs 20 p per kW h. Calculate the cost.
A 12 V supply is connected to a 4.0 Ω and a 8.0 Ω resistor in series. Calculate the current and the p.d. across the 8.0 Ω resistor.
Explain why the total resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than either resistor.
short.model: Current has more than one path, so more charge can flow for the same p.d.; the total current is larger, so the combined resistance (V ÷ I) is smaller.
points: greater supply current for same p.d.

short.q: Explain how a fuse and an earth wire together protect a user if a fault makes a metal casing live.
short.model: The casing is connected to earth, so a large current flows through the earth wire, heating the fuse wire until it melts. This disconnects the appliance so the user cannot get a shock.

short.q: State two advantages of connecting house lamps in parallel rather than in series.
short.model: Each lamp has the full supply p.d. so is bright; each can be switched on and off independently (and one failing doesn't turn the others off).
